purpose: Close ASVS V5.2.2 (L1) on the attachment upload route, which selected the parser purely from the filename extension. Untrusted bytes reached zipEntry, extractPdf, ExcelJS and an external OCR process on the strength of a string the sender controls, and the mediaType in the response was echoed straight back from the client-declared file.type. Adds content-signature validation before dispatch and derives the media type server-side.
requiredInvariants: No new dependency. The check compares leading bytes; nothing is installed and no licence question is opened.

The claim is not overstated for text formats. Plain text has no signature, so the module does not pretend to verify one: it verifies the checkable inverse, that a text extension does not carry a recognised binary container. That limit is written in the module, in the register note and in the tests.
The existing limits are untouched: 4 files, 8 MB per file, 24 MB total, 30 s OCR timeout, 4 PDF pages. None is relaxed to accommodate the new check.
The extractors are not rewritten. The check runs before them and rejects through the response's existing rejected[] field, so the POST handler needs no change.
The control is verified by tests bound to behaviour, not to its presence: neutralising the check fails 19 of 47 cases.
The spec is added to the CI web-unit job. A test CI never runs would not guard the control, and CI runs five named files rather than the suite.
Only the ci.yml web-unit test list changes. No gate logic, no other job, and the action-pinning ratchet stays at exit 0.
apps/landing is not touched. No production, REG.RU, DNS or database mutation.

The cryptographic inventory is regenerated by scripts/security/discover-cryptography.mjs only, never edited by hand. Adding content-signature.ts raises the tracked-source count the inventory records from 2150 to 2151, which the 'committed inventory is not stale' test compares exactly. Nothing else moves: the new module performs no cryptography, so no operation or key-material entry changes.
acceptance: A file whose extension disagrees with its content is rejected with CONTENT_TYPE_MISMATCH:<ext> before any parser sees it.
mediaType in the response is derived from the verified extension, never copied from the client's file.type.
pnpm --filter @pc/web typecheck passes; the new spec passes 47/47 and fails 19/47 with the control neutralised.
The full web suite is unchanged against main: the same 237 failing files and 397 failing tests appear on main before this branch, with 47 additional passing tests here and nothing newly broken.
V5.2.2 moves FAIL to PASS with five self-revoking conditions, all 7 negative checks revoke, and the register rebuilds at applied 332 / rejected 0 with FAIL falling from 121 to 120.
node --test scripts/security/*.test.mjs passes, including the committed-inventory staleness check.
